Zoot Sweepstakes Casino Closing Player-Facing Platform

Published November 11, 2026 · 4 min read · By the OddsLighthouse Editorial Team

Zoot Sweepstakes Casino is shutting down its player-facing platform, parent company Enigma Lake Holdings announced, as the business shifts its focus toward supplying games to other operators rather than running its own sweepstakes casino. Covers.com reported the closure, which comes with a detailed, multi-week wind-down schedule rather than an immediate shutoff.

Why Zoot is closing

According to Covers.com, Enigma Lake is redirecting its business toward Zoot Studios, a game-development arm that supplies titles to third-party platforms rather than operating its own consumer-facing casino. The report doesn't cite any regulatory action against Zoot as a factor in the decision — this is a company pivoting its business model, not a platform being forced offline by a state regulator.

The closure timeline

Covers.com laid out a specific, multi-stage schedule for players still holding balances on the platform, all times Eastern:

Date (2026, ET)What happens
Nov. 12, 11:59 p.m.Deadline for mail-in Sweepstake Coin redemption requests
Nov. 16Valid mail-in redemption requests credited
Nov. 20, 11:59 p.m.Games become inaccessible; Gold Coins and unmet-playthrough Sweepstake Coins expire
Nov. 24, 11:59 p.m.Deadline for prize redemption requests
Nov. 30, 5:00 p.m.All player accounts permanently close

Alongside that schedule, Zoot lowered its minimum redemption threshold from $100 to $10 and removed weekly redemption limits and processing fees for the wind-down period, with each eligible Sweepstake Coin valued at $1. The Coin Store has already closed, and new registrations, tournaments, and leaderboards are suspended.

If you have a Zoot balance: Covers.com reports that eligible balances of at least $10 that can't be paid out before the platform closes can still be claimed by contacting customer support through May 31, 2027, with support staying available for complaints, balance claims, and data requests through at least November 30, 2027.

What else is happening in sweepstakes casino gaming

Zoot's exit comes as at least one competitor is leaning further into the sweepstakes model: Covers.com's report notes that ClubWPT Gold, the World Poker Tour's sweepstakes poker room, is running a $5 million free-entry tournament that drew more than 100,000 entries in its first week and runs through November 28, with the operator aiming to challenge the entry-count record set by GGPoker's October 2026 event, which drew 420,084 entries. The contrast underscores that Zoot's closure reflects a company-specific strategic shift rather than a broader retreat from the sweepstakes casino category.
